transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Marisol. How can I help you this evening?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi, yeah. My internet keeps cutting out again. It's out right now, actually, I'm calling from my mobile.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that, let's get it looked at. Can I start with the account number and the PIN on the account, please?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yep. It's 3308-115-472, and the PIN is 6014.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And the name on the account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Daniel Okafor.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks, Daniel, you're verified. So tell me what's been happening.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So most evenings, the internet just drops. Everything goes. It'll be out for maybe two or three minutes, sometimes five, and then it comes back on its own. It happens three or four times a night. And it went again about ten minutes ago, and it's still out now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. So just to make sure I've got it: most evenings the whole connection drops out, for anywhere from two to five minutes, three or four times a night, it comes back by itself, and right now it's down again. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, that's it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. How long has this been happening?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: About three weeks now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Three weeks, got it. Does it happen on wired devices as well, or only on WiFi?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both. My gaming PC is plugged straight into the modem and it drops too. And the WiFi on the phones goes at the same time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's really useful, because it tells me it's not a WiFi problem, it's the connection coming into the house. What lights do you see on the modem right now, while it's down?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look. The power light is solid. The one with the globe is blinking orange, and the WiFi one is solid white.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, a blinking orange globe means the modem has lost its signal from our network and is trying to reconnect. When it's working normally, is the globe solid white?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, solid white.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Have you noticed if it's around the same time each evening, or random?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It starts around seven, I'd say. During the day I'm at work so I couldn't tell you, but on weekends it seems fine in the mornings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, that's good to know. And has anything changed in the house around three weeks ago? Any new equipment, anyone working on the wiring, anything moved around the modem?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Not that I can think of. We had the living room painted about a month ago, but that's it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I'll keep that in mind. Now, I can see on my side that the modem is offline at the moment, which matches what you're seeing. What I'd like to do is run a line test, which checks the signal between your modem and our equipment in the street. It takes about two to three minutes. Would it be okay if I place you on a brief hold while it runs?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, no problem.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Daniel. I'll be back with you in about a minute.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Daniel, thanks for holding. The test is about halfway through, so I just need another minute or so. Are you still okay to hold?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, that's fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, I'll be right back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks so much for waiting. Okay, I have the results. The line from the street to your house is testing fine, but the signal arriving at your modem is weak and very noisy, and it's dipping in and out. That pattern usually points to something inside the house, like a loose connection or a splitter on the cable before it reaches the modem.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A splitter? I don't think we have one of those.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It might be one you've never noticed. It's a small metal piece, about the size of a matchbox, with one cable going in and two or three coming out. They're often behind the TV unit or where the cable comes through the wall. And how long has this been happening for, roughly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Like I said, about three weeks now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, sorry, three weeks. Could you follow the cable back from the modem and see where it goes?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, hang on. It goes along the skirting board... into the back of the TV cabinet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh. Okay, there is something here. A little metal box, behind the cabinet. One cable from the wall, and then two coming out. One goes to the modem and the other one isn't connected to anything, it's just lying there.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the splitter, and the loose cable going nowhere is a good clue. Can you check whether the connectors are screwed on tightly? Especially the one coming from the wall.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hmm. The one from the wall is quite loose actually. It spins if I touch it. And the one that's just lying there isn't connected at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. An open port and a loose connector can let in a lot of interference, and evenings are when there's the most noise on the cable network, which would explain why it drops at night. Did the painters move the TV cabinet when they were doing the living room?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh. Yeah, they did. They moved everything out and put it back. They probably knocked it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That would fit the timing nicely, about a month ago, and then the drops starting soon after. Here's what I'd suggest. Since the second cable isn't going to anything, we can take the splitter out completely and connect the cable from the wall straight to the modem. Fewer connections means less to go wrong. Do you have anything else that uses that other cable, like an old TV box?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We used to have a TV box but we sent it back last year. So no, nothing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Then the splitter isn't doing anything useful. Do you need it for anything else, or are you happy to take it out?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Happy to take it out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. So, first, unscrew the cable that goes from the splitter to the modem, at the splitter end, and then unscrew the one from the wall. Then take the end of the wall cable and screw it directly onto the back of the modem, where the other cable was. Make sure it's finger tight. Take your time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, give me a minute.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, the splitter's out. The wall cable is going straight into the modem now. It's tight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Does the cable from the wall reach the modem okay, without being stretched?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, there's enough slack.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Now the modem needs to resync with the network. Let's give it a restart so it starts fresh. Could you hold the power button on the back for about two seconds until the lights go off, then press it again to turn it on?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, it's off... and back on. All the lights are flashing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's normal, it takes about two minutes to come up. While it does, I'll explain what I'm going to look for. Once it's online, I'll check the signal level and the noise level on my side, and compare them with what we saw in the line test. If the splitter was the problem, we should see a big improvement straight away.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In the meantime, I've added a note to your account about the splitter and the painting, so if anyone else looks at your account they'll know what we found tonight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. I called last week and they told me it was an outage in the area and to wait, and it just kept happening.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Honestly it's been really annoying. I work late shifts from home some nights, and I've been booted off my work system in the middle of things, and I lose online games in the middle of a match.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand, that's really frustrating, especially when you were told to just wait it out. There was a small outage in your area last week, which might be why they said that, but it was fixed on the Thursday, and your drops continued after that. So I'm glad you called back so we could look at it properly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, me too.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, the globe light's gone solid white.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, and I can see the modem online now. Let me check the numbers. Okay, this is a big improvement. The signal level has gone up a lot, and the noise has dropped right down. Earlier, the signal to noise was around twenty-two, which is poor, and now it's sitting at thirty-eight, which is excellent.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, nice.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does it happen on your wired devices as well, the drops?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, I mentioned the gaming PC drops too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's right, yes. Could you run a speed test on the gaming PC for me, since it's wired? It'll give us the cleanest reading.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure. Okay... 487 down, 22 up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's right in line with your 500 megabit plan. Before tonight, I can see the modem was only managing around 150 when it was connected, because of all the errors on the line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That would explain the lag in games, too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. With that much noise, the modem keeps resending data, so even when it's connected everything feels sluggish. Now, because the drops normally happen a few times an evening, I'd like to keep an eye on the line for a few minutes while we're still on the phone. If you could leave something running, like a video or a download, that would help.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, I'll put a video on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. While that runs, I'll set up a 48-hour monitor on your line. It records the signal every few minutes. If it sees the signal drop or the noise come back, it automatically flags it to us and we'll contact you, so you won't need to call in again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that's good.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And just so you know what to expect: if the drops do come back even with the splitter gone, the next step would be a technician visit to check the wall socket and the cable outside, and that would be free of charge, since it's on our side of the line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. Good to know.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How's the video looking?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine, it's playing in HD with no buffering.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. On my side, the signal has stayed steady the whole time, and there haven't been any errors since the modem came back on. That's about ten minutes now, which is longer than it's been stable on any evening this week.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, normally it would have gone again by now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: One more tip. If you ever do need a splitter again, for example if you get a TV box in the future, just give us a call and we'll send you a proper one with the right caps for the unused ports. Those cheaper ones without caps tend to pick up a lot of noise.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll remember that. I think that splitter came with the house, to be honest.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's quite common. Okay, so before we finish, can you confirm everything is working for you now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, it's been solid since we took that thing out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, then I'm happy we've resolved it tonight. I've put the notes and the line monitor on the account, and if it flags anything we'll be in touch. Anything else I can help you with tonight?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything. Thanks for your help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're welcome, Daniel. Enjoy the rest of your evening, and enjoy the gaming.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ha, thanks. Bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for calling S-Net, have a great night. Bye.
